KMZ-FIX-88.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 29 (Evaluation, Characterization, and Glazing), p. 825

KMZ-FIX-116.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 5 (Periodontal Considerations), p. 154

SAUD-1835.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 19 (Framework Design and Metal Selection for Metal-Ceramic Restorations), p. 577

R19-Fixed-4.n: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics 6e: the biologic width is measured by sounding to bone with a probe under local anesthesia (p. 154), and a bitewing radiograph can confirm a violation (p. 159). Both a probe and a bitewing are reasonable, so check which one your key expects.

R19-Fixed-27.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 4 (Principles of Occlusion), p. 134
R19-Fixed-27.ans: full coverage with anterior posterior contact
R19-Fixed-27.c: Corrected per Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics 6e p. 134: an occlusal device covers the arch with even contact from all opposing teeth in centric relation, plus anterior guidance in excursions. A device with no contact doesn't protect the teeth.

R19-Fixed-34.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 29 (Evaluation, Characterization, and Glazing), p. 820
R19-Fixed-34.n: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics 6e p. 820: proximal contacts are checked first at try-in, because an overcontoured (too heavy) contact is the usual reason a finished crown won't seat when the metal coping did.

SAL-555.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 2 (Diagnostic Procedures), p. 68
SAL-555.c: Corrected per Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics 6e p. 68: a slide forward and up from centric relation comes from contacts on the mesial inclines of maxillary cusps (and distal inclines of mandibular cusps). On a new upper crown you adjust its mesial incline. This matches SAL-260.

SAL-560.ref: Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed., ch. 4 (Principles of Occlusion), p. 116
SAL-560.c: Corrected: soreness with premature contacts after treatment points to excessive vertical dimension, which means a decreased freeway (interocclusal rest) space. A decreased vertical dimension gives the opposite (excess freeway space). This matches KMZ-FIX-124 and S05-Q78-A.

SEP-Sultan-40.n: ⚠ A fracture running from the mesial to the distal marginal ridge with a mobile segment describes a split tooth, which is usually extracted (or the mobile segment removed). A core and crown suits a cracked tooth whose segments are not separable. Check this one.

JA-Jul-56.n: ⚠ The November bank (NOVA-26) and most pedo texts protect an erupted dens evaginatus (sealant/composite or gradual reduction) rather than just monitoring, because the tubercle fractures easily and exposes the pulp horn.

SAUD-865.n: ⚠ The same recall appears in the Salem bank (SAL-263) with "mobile crown" as the answer. Metallic taste with pain after a cast post, with no mobility or radiolucency, is debated between a loose crown leaking and an early vertical root fracture.

SAL-263.n: ⚠ The same recall appears in the Saudi bank (SAUD-865) with "vertical root fracture" as the answer. Check which your key expects.
